chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The testator has the right to retract his will, whether he is in good health or in illness.'

key_terms.لِلْمُوصِي: The testator (one who makes a will)

ai.seo_question: Can a person change or revoke their will after writing it but before dying?
ai.summary: Reported by Ubayd ibn Zurara from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith clarifies that the right of revocation (ruju') in a will is not restricted by the testator's health status, thereby affirming the flexibility of testamentary disposition in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling ensures that a person can alter their final wishes whether in robust health or during the critical period of illness (marad al-mawt), reflecting the principle that the will remains provisional until death. It underscores the legal capacity of the testator to manage their estate dynamically, a key aspect of Shia inheritance law derived from the Imams' teachings.
